title: Counter-Selector Wave 20: exception intervention, self-falsification, and custody counterevidence
purpose: Try to break the strongest live Counter-Selector trace. Audit Elliot Richardson's Nicaragua record for person-attributable exception intervention, distinguish retrospective self-critique from model elasticity, preserve team and status support, record custody failures, and update the graph-inert external-review export without contacting anyone or authorizing CS-FT-01.

new_support_assignments.basis: In the attributed oral-history record, Richardson describes obtaining an equal-access commitment for the opposition, securing removal of incumbent-party signs from government property, preparing Sandinista lieutenants for the possibility of defeat, and joining the election-night appeal for Ortega to accept the evident result. These are specific interventions at media, state-resource, expectation, and succession gates rather than the mere fact of holding an unprecedented mission title.

interventions.person_action: raised unequal access with Ortega and reports obtaining a commitment to equality of access
challenged party signs on government property and reports that Ortega removed them
worked before election day to frame acceptance of defeat as the larger and more durable act
joined Carter in appealing for acceptance of the evident outcome and immediately sent Ortega a transition-framing letter after concession

new_support_assignments.ceiling: The support is bounded to specific attributed interventions in one election-transition artifact. It does not prove that Richardson caused the concession, authored the mission's distributed safeguards, controlled every relevant gate, or could reproduce the operation without the professional ONUVEN staff, Jimmy Carter, the electoral council, and other institutional actors.

team_mechanisms_not_person_support.reason: the transcript describes a mission-wide system operated by regional representatives; it is not assigned solely to Richardson
official UN context describes hundreds of observers and radio-satellite coordination; scale is collective support
the successful institutional control system is not converted into sole person authorship

indicators.indicator: Richardson says Humberto and Daniel Ortega were more responsible and responsive than he had expected
Richardson says he may have let the UN team down by not challenging Carter's dominant final-press-conference role and wonders whether he chickened out

model_elasticity_adjudication.reason: The record shows retrospective updating and self-critique, but not a contemporaneous contradiction entering Richardson's model, producing an attributable changed decision, preserving the relationship, and improving a recoverable object. Model elasticity therefore remains unresolved.

observed_support: selection for high public reputation and credibility
formal appointment as the Secretary-General's personal representative
a professional ONUVEN mission led operationally by Iqbal Riza
hundreds of international observers and distributed communications
cooperation from the Supreme Electoral Council
parallel participation by Jimmy Carter and other international actors
prior Cabinet, diplomatic, legal, and Law of the Sea experience
support_context.reason: No matched resource-normalized comparator shows output exceeding what this authority, reputation, staff, logistics, and institutional access would predict.

counterevidence.item: Richardson says he did not know whether a copy of the Spanish-language letter to Ortega was made and the interviewer had not found it in the UN files
counterevidence.effect: the intervention object was not preserved as an independently inspectable custody receipt

counterevidence.item: No direct Law of the Sea successor state-package receipt or recipient acknowledgment was acquired
counterevidence.effect: successor-capable institutional continuity remains narrower than direct person-to-person handoff

countermodels: retrospective self-report may overattribute collective mission work
Ortega may have conceded because of vote totals, domestic politics, or other international actors rather than Richardson's intervention
Richardson's high reputation and access may explain his ability to secure meetings and commitments
Iqbal Riza and the professional ONUVEN staff may account for most operational exception handling
the missing letter copy weakens custody and causal inspection
self-critique can coexist with failure to repair
a successful novel mission does not establish support-adjusted surplus
one election transition does not establish universal exception handling

negative_controls.finding: The novelty and prestige of ONUVEN do not themselves support exception handling. Support attaches only to the four attributed interventions.
Admitting that he may have failed to challenge Carter is epistemically useful counterevidence, but no resulting repair, handoff, or changed object is observed.
A large professional mission, formal authority, high reputation, and cooperating institutions prevent the mission outcome from becoming a support-adjusted-surplus finding.

sources.title: Yale-UN Oral History: Elliot Richardson interview, 7 October 1997
sources.record_state: full transcript parsed from a 23-page PDF; screenshot requests failed at the transport cache and are not treated as visual verification
supports: Richardson describes seeking equal opposition access to state broadcasting and obtaining Ortega's commitment
Richardson describes objecting to incumbent-party signs on government property and says Ortega had them removed
Richardson describes an election-night appeal with Jimmy Carter for Ortega to accept the evident result
Richardson describes writing an immediate Spanish-language letter framing concession as a durable democratic transition
Richardson credits Iqbal Riza and the ONUVEN staff and describes the mission's distributed complaint and observation mechanisms
limits: the interview occurred more than seven years after the election and is retrospective self-report
the transcript does not establish that Richardson's appeal caused Ortega's concession
the letter to Ortega was not retained in the files identified by the interviewer and Richardson did not remember making a copy
the mission's successful mechanisms were collective and cannot be assigned solely to Richardson
parsed PDF text is not a substitute for successful page-image inspection

review_questions: Do the four person-attributable Nicaragua interventions justify bounded exception handling after collective mission contributions are removed?
Does the retrospective interview overattribute causality or operational authorship?
Does the missing letter copy materially narrow custody?
Do the two retrospective update indicators remain below model-elasticity threshold?
Does the high-support ledger defeat support-adjusted surplus?
countermodels: mission success may be primarily institutional and team produced
Ortega's concession may not be causally attributable to the subject
retrospective self-report may compress or misallocate roles
high status and formal access may explain the observed interventions
falsifiers: the transcript does not attribute the access, sign-removal, or election-night interventions to the subject
a contemporaneous record contradicts the subject's account
the subject's actions occurred only after the relevant state transition was already secured
the mission's operational staff, not the subject, controlled every cited intervention
a retained letter or recipient acknowledgment materially changes the custody finding

next_action: Acquire the exact contemporaneous Nicaragua letters and acknowledgments through non-contact public or archival access; submit the identity-label-removed export to a genuinely independent reviewer only under separate authorization; and refuse CS-FT-01 until model elasticity, support normalization, direct handoff, and independent review are established.
